parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.lead: Two metal cubes P and Q are in thermal contact with each other.
parts.text:
P and Q are in thermal equilibrium.

State what is meant by the term thermal equilibrium.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Data for P and Q are given in Table 3.1.

[[fig:f1]]

P and Q are initially both at the same temperature.

P is supplied with 24 kJ of thermal energy. After some time, P and Q are once again both at the same temperature as each other.

P and Q are perfectly insulated from the surroundings.

Determine the change in temperature Δ*T* of Q.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Nitrogen may be assumed to be an ideal gas. A fixed amount of nitrogen gas is contained at a constant pressure of 1.6 × 10⁵ Pa.

The variation of the volume *V* of the gas with the temperature *θ* of the gas is shown in Fig. 3.1.

[[fig:f2]]
parts.text:
The temperature of the nitrogen gas is increased from 0 °C to 210 °C.
Determine the work done on the gas.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the number *N* of molecules of nitrogen gas.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The mass of a nitrogen molecule is 4.7 × 10⁻²⁶ kg.

Calculate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) speed of a nitrogen molecule at 210 °C.

figures.caption: Table 3.1
figures.alt: A table gives specific heat capacity and mass for cubes P and Q: specific heat capacity is 390 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for P and 910 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ for Q; mass is 0.54 kg for P and 0.37 kg for Q.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.1
figures.alt: A graph of volume V in m³ against temperature θ in °C, with a straight rising line from approximately 0.18 m³ at 0 °C to 0.38 m³ at 300 °C.
